answer: Picture a flock of birds crossing one wide horizon: each bird may fly only in its own wedge of sky, and its voice counts only when birds from far-apart wedges vouch for it. A plume of fresh masks hatched in a single wedge can vouch for each other, yet their combined weight is capped by the narrow cut between their wedge and the rest — ten clones in one corner weigh as one voice. To gain more, the farmer must wander into many distant wedges and earn trust in each, paying tenfold the time and ties. One honest agent, one wedge, keeps the wage his own seasons earned.
